fact: IPC shadow trade minister Rodney Cloete told the Windhoek Observer that Namibia has no data protection statute, so no legal definition of a data controller and no cross-border transfer rules; this is an opposition MP's statement, dated by the article's publication date.
ICT minister Emma Theofelus said Namibia is finalising the Data Protection Bill, speaking at the first meeting of the new CRAN board on the Monday before the 14 July 2026 article.

Minister Theofelus said the Data Protection Bill had been through consultation and drafting and was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation for validation and onward processing by Parliament; she spoke at a staff engagement the day before the 27 January 2026 article.

Minister Theofelus said the Data Protection Bill, about 12 years in preparation, was expected to be tabled in Parliament the following month; IPPR's Frederico Links said the public had not seen the latest version; she spoke the week before the 17 August 2025 article.
Minister Theofelus said at the Standard Bank Anti-Financial Crime Conference that the government would introduce the Data Protection Bill to be tabled in September 2025.

The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology, through Minister Emma Theofelus, said on 14 August 2025 that it would table a Data Protection Bill in September 2025; the article gives no sign the bill had yet been tabled.

The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology published a revised 59-page draft Data Protection Bill for comment, dated 2022 (month March taken from the publisher's filename, not the text), with the gazette notice number left blank.
The revised draft's long title provides for establishing a Data Protection Supervisory Authority and its powers, duties and functions; this is a draft and no body is stated as constituted.

The document is an undated 26-page draft Data Protection Bill from the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology, identified from IPPR's description as the 2020 version (year inferred, with February 2020 given by IPPR as the stakeholder engagement); it carries no bill number or gazette front matter and its copy ends mid-Part, before any commencement or repeal provision.
Section 25 of the 2020 draft establishes the Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia, with Part VII running to section 37; as a draft, no body is stated as constituted.

Two named analysts writing in a personal capacity describe Namibia's Data Protection Bill as a draft that proposes a supervisory authority, with Namibia still lacking a comprehensive data protection framework.
New Era reports the ICT ministry is finalising the Data Protection Bill.
The Speaker of the National Assembly said Namibia is finalising a Data Protection Bill to ensure personal privacy and data security.
The Brief names the Data Protection Bill of 2023 as complementary legislation on data privacy, without saying it is enacted.
The ICT ministry's Frans Nghitila said Namibia has formulated a draft Data Protection Bill.
Commentator Hafeni Kashimbonde refers to 'Data Protection Bills in Namibia' as the country's national privacy protection, with no law in force named.
